questions.prompt: Which of these is quantitative data?
questions.explanation: Quantitative data uses numbers: 10 minutes. Salty and red are describing words, so they are qualitative.

questions.prompt: Which of these is qualitative data?
questions.explanation: Soft describes a quality with a word. 4 legs and 6 m are numbers, so they are quantitative.

questions.prompt: The number of pupils in a class is...
questions.explanation: You count pupils in whole numbers, so it is discrete. You cannot have half a pupil.

questions.prompt: Which of these is continuous data?
options: The number of books on a shelf
The number of goals in a match
questions.explanation: Height is measured and can be any value, like 1.40 m. Goals and books are counted, so they are discrete.

questions.prompt: A farmer writes: 12 hens, 3.5 kg of beans, 2 cows. Which one is continuous data?
questions.explanation: Mass is measured and can have decimals. Hens and cows are counted in whole numbers.

questions.prompt: Why is the number of cars at the market discrete data?
options: Because you count cars in whole numbers
Because cars can be measured in metres
questions.explanation: Discrete data is counted and has no values in between. There is no such thing as 10 and a half cars.
